title: Take a bike light off its handlebar bracket with the release lever held down, switch it off and put it in the bowl
instruction: Take the light off the handlebar, switch it off and put it in the bowl.
context: A front bike light rides a rail on a clamp round the handlebar, and a sprung catch holds it there: it comes off only while the catch's lever is held down, so one hand holds the lever down while the other slides the light off; pulled without the lever held, it does not come. Whoever rides to work or school does this whenever the bike is left outside, or the light is gone, and takes the light in to charge it. Here the real bar, stem, bracket and light stand at true height over the bench; the rest of the bike is left out because nothing in the job touches it. Two hands must work at one small part without meeting, one pressing a tab of 10 x 8 mm behind the light while the other draws the light forward along its rail; then the light is switched off by holding its button for a second and put into a bowl.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left; heights over the bench. A straight flat handlebar, 600 mm wide, 31.8 mm at the middle (for instance Ritchey Comp flat bar), its axis along y at x 24, 8 cm over the bench, held at its middle by a 70 mm stem on a steerer stub in a wooden block 60 x 60 x 40 mm screwed to the bench at x 17, as a bike's stem holds it. A CatEye H-34N FlexTight bracket (part 5338827N) tightened on the bar 7 cm left of the stem, its rail along x. On it a CatEye Volt 400 front light (HL-EL461RC; 108 x 31 x 31 mm, about 120 g), pointing away from the arms, switched on, caught at the rail's end; its release lever is a tab of about 10 x 8 mm under the rail's rear end. A Fiesta small bowl (item 460, Lapis; 143 mm across, 48 mm high), loose, at x 38, y +20. Nothing varies by seed: every seed gives this start (under the harness --seed 0 runs as trial seed 1415158438, the same start). Start check: the light clicked onto the rail, its indicator lit, the bowl on its mark (within 5 mm).
scoring: Read from the end state. 1.0: the light lies in the bowl, switched off; bracket and bar where they were; both grippers 3 cm clear of the light; the light at rest (under 2 cm/s over 0.25 s); all of this held for 1 s. 0.75: the light in the bowl but still on, or off but with a gripper within 3 cm of it or still moving; or switched off and lying on the bench within 15 cm of the bowl's rim. 0.5: the light wholly off the rail, anywhere on the bench. 0.25: the light freed from its catch (slid 5 mm or more towards the rail's end) but still on the rail. 0: still caught; or the light off the bench. Real bench: look into the bowl and at the light's lens and indicator; a mark on the rail 5 mm from the light's caught place; a ruler from the bowl's rim.
reset_notes: Switch the light on, slide it onto the rail until the catch clicks, put the bowl on its mark: about 20 s.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at true size. The catch is a sprung tab: while it is pressed 2 mm or more the light slides along the rail against 3 N; let go, it stops within 0.5 mm of where the next 20 Hz step finds it. The light is set free at the first 20 Hz step past 30 mm of slide. The switch is a sprung button that turns the light off when held down for 1 s. Lever, rail and button forces assumed until measured on the bought parts. Not modelled: the bar's roundness under the band, rubber parts, the beam.
